assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to degrade proteins rather than inhibit them is a genuinely new pharmacological principle and fits my own bar of a game-changer with real consequences: degraders are in clinical trials and the molecular-glue mechanism of thalidomide-type drugs was explained chemically. Conceptually simple and chemically elegant.
assessment.attribution: PROTAC concept and first proof (Crews, Deshaies with Sakamoto), then VHL-based small-molecule PROTACs and structure-guided design (Ciulli, Crews). Cereblon/molecular-glue work (Handa, Ito, Gray and others) is a separate strand that crowds a three-person limit; Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli is a defensible but not unique configuration.
assessment.maturity: About 25 years from the original concept, with many independent groups and a deep clinical pipeline, but no approved PROTAC yet; timing is good but arguably early on the medical-outcome side.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on PROTACs or on molecular glues and cereblon biology
Priority between Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto, Ciulli and the Handa/Ito group
Clinical validation still pending

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another by chemistry on DNA without double-strand cleavage, a clearly new capability built from deaminase chemistry plus protein engineering and already used in therapies and clinical trials. Strong consequences and very clear originality.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu is the decisive inventor and the lab that created both cytosine and adenine base editors (Komor, Gaudelli as trainees, with a Kondo/Nishida parallel cytosine deaminase approach). A single-laureate or Liu plus one scenario is credible; I would keep it with Liu alone to avoid contested allocation.
assessment.maturity: Introduced 2016-2017, rapidly and independently reproduced, first clinical results in hand; recognition is timely though still young relative to typical prize lag.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as chemistry rather than medicine or genome engineering
Overlap with prime editing and CRISPR, which was already recognized in 2020
Treatment of the Kondo/Nishida contribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs that add nonstandard amino acids to proteins in living cells expanded the genetic code in a way that gives chemists atomic-level control of proteins; wide use in probes, therapeutics and engineered organisms. Close to my ribosome and translation interests.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang made the first genetically encoded unnatural amino acid in E. coli and yeast; Chin extended it to eukaryotes and to quadruplet codons and recoded genomes. Mehl and Yokoyama contributed meaningfully, so a three-person limit forces hard choices.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation across many labs and routine use; mature, though the full recoded-organism program is still developing.
uncertainties: Allocation among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama
Whether Schultz's early synthetic-biology claims dominate perception over the detailed enabling steps

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N coupling is arguably the most practised reaction in medicinal-chemistry synthesis, making amine arylation straightforward and general. It is a very clear game-changer in daily use, in the same spirit as the 2010 cross-coupling prize and click chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general ligand-controlled catalytic systems; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor but not the general method. Two-person attribution is clean.
assessment.maturity: Very mature with decades of independent use; recognition is late if anything. The main concern is perceived overlap with the 2010 palladium coupling prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a sufficiently distinct advance after the 2010 prize
Credit of earlier Migita/Kosugi stannyl amine chemistry

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The funnel energy-landscape picture resolved Levinthal's paradox and unified statistical-mechanical theory with quantitative experimental folding kinetics; theory that connects to experiment is exactly what I value. Its influence on protein physics and on modern structure prediction is deep.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic (with Bryngelson) built the landscape theory; Fersht's phi-value analysis provided the key experimental mapping. Dill's contributions on hydrophobic collapse and lattice models overlap, so allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Over 30 years of confirmation; the framework is stable. Recognition is mature, though the AlphaFold prize in 2024 may have diminished the sense of unfinished business.
uncertainties: Allocation among Wolynes, Onuchic, Fersht, Dill and Bryngelson
Whether a theory-plus-experiment pairing is judged as a single coherent discovery

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of intracellular compartmentation is a genuinely new concept (P granules, nucleolus, signalling condensates) and has changed how cell biologists and physical chemists think about cellular organization.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman established P granules as liquids, Rosen showed multivalent-interaction phase separation in vitro; Pappu and Mittag supplied the physical-chemistry framework. The group is large and the contribution split is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Roughly 15 years old, already hugely influential, but the physiological significance and the boundaries of the claims are still debated, so it may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Debate over which condensates are truly phase-separated in vivo
Chemistry versus cell-biology or medicine placement
Allocation among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned potentials give near quantum accuracy at classical cost, and are transforming atomistic simulation of reactions, materials and condensed phases. I value computation that reproduces quantitative experiment, and this is where simulation is moving.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello introduced neural-network potentials; Csányi and Bartók developed Gaussian-approximation potentials; von Lilienfeld and E also contributed. Parrinello's separate ab initio MD and metadynamics work complicates his role.
assessment.maturity: Fast-growing and increasingly validated, but transferability, data requirements and foundation-model generalization are still unsettled; recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Whether the field has stabilized enough after the rapid foundation-model shift
Overlap with Car-Parrinello and metadynamics candidates for Parrinello
Which of the many methods should be named

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Descriptor-based computational catalyst design, including d-band and scaling relations, made catalysis predictions quantitative and led to experimentally validated new catalysts for ammonia, hydrogen evolution and methanol. This is theory that visibly changed an experimental field.
assessment.attribution: Nørskov is the clear intellectual driver; Mavrikakis, Rossmeisl, Jaramillo and Scheffler were important collaborators or parallel contributors, but a single laureate best reflects the leadership.
assessment.maturity: Decades of experimental confirmation, though scaling-relation limits and DFT accuracy are acknowledged caveats; mature.
uncertainties: Single laureate versus combined prize with an experimental partner
Systematic DFT-functional error limiting predictiveness
Overlap with an earlier DFT-related prize in perception
